text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate on /api/generate - 512 alerts/min across prod-us-east - paging group: paged
sara (oncall): got it, I'm on. looking at traces + dashboards now
michael: taking DB side - any idea if this is real traffic spike or a noisy alert? can you paste the raw rule? @sara
sara (oncall): rule is `http_5xx_rate > 5% for 1m` across service:inference, route:/api/generate
sara (oncall): initial look: lots of 502/504 from backend model pool, but errors are very bursty and concentrated in a few nodes
raj: I'm seeing a correlated spike in request latencies from bucketized metrics, looks like cold kv-cache misses. probably transient
liz: customers? any user-facing incidents reported yet? support channel is quiet
sara (oncall): no public tickets yet, but we should assume partial degradations for long-running chat sessions
michael: ok planning live mitigation: 1) suppress duplicate PD entries (they're flooding ops) 2) temp rate-limit the alert to 1/min 3) implement grouping key by upstream_host + model_variant
sara (oncall): to confirm: we want a temporary dedupe/rate limit at Alertmanager level. I can flip a gate if someone gives the exact command
monitoring-bot: Grafana link: https://grafana.internal/d/ABC123/inference-errors?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now
sara (oncall): clicking graphs. yep these three hosts (host-12/14/19) are generating 80% of the noise
michael: i'll push a quick routing change to avoid the problematic hosts from the pool for new requests
sara (oncall): while michael does that, i'll create a temporary PD dedupe rule: `squelch: rate:1m, group_by: upstream_host, fingerprint: service+route` — want to run it now?
raj: +1 run it. also let's add a 5m cooldown to avoid flipflopping
sara (oncall): executing: `alertmanagerctl apply --squelch "service:inference" --rate 1/m --group-by upstream_host --cooldown 5m` (dry-run shown below)

# dry-run output
would create squelch rule: id=tmp-202403, scope=service:inference, rate=1/m, keys=[upstream_host], cooldown=5m

sara (oncall): applying now
incident-bot: ACTION: Temporary squelch rule tmp-202403 applied by sara (oncall)
michael: rerouting done: drain host-12/14/19 from pool, new requests go to healthy nodes
monitoring-bot: rolling error-rate avg dropping. 5m window shows 60% reduction in redundant alerts
liz: nice. can we also change the threshold to be less sensitive while we investigate? 1m eval is noisy
raj: propose change: `http_5xx_rate > 8% for 3m` for this route as a temporary mitigation. that'll reduce false positives while retaining signal
sara (oncall): proposed and applied via AlertRule quickpatch: `PATCH /alerting/rules/744` payload: `{"expr":"http_5xx_rate > 0.08","for":"3m"}`
monitoring-bot: Rule 744 updated. new thresholds active
michael: FYI I re-ran model pool health check; one node's kv-cache was thrashing due to bad sharding config. logged a fix, rolling out a patch to the runtime
sara (oncall): handoff: @oncall-next you'll take over in 25m. I'll leave squelch + rule changes active for now. if errors re-emerge, escalate to eng-runtime
oncall-next: ack. i'll watch the dashboard and PD console
liz: customers: I'm pinging support to proactively notify any users on long-lived sessions. copy of message posted to #support
sara (oncall): doc-ing the temporary changes in the incident channel: short summary + links

Summary of live mitigation:
- Applied Alertmanager squelch tmp-202403 scope=service:inference rate=1/m group_by=upstream_host cooldown=5m
- Increased threshold for /api/generate to 8% over 3m (rule 744)
- Drained problematic hosts from model pool (host-12/14/19)
- Runtime shard fix in progress by michael
- Notified support & CDN teams

raj: follow-up tasks (created as tickets):
- IR-342: analyze root cause of kv-cache thrash and fix sharding (assigned michael)
- IR-343: add smarter grouping keys to alerts (include model_variant, instance_id) (assigned sara)
- IR-344: add a dedicated error-rate dashboard panel for route-level grouping (assigned liz)
sara (oncall): can one of you add a longer-term dedupe policy in Alertmanager that persists? tmp rule will auto-expire in 6h
michael: i'll open PR with proposed alertmanager config: change `group_by` to ["service","route","model_variant"] and add `dedupe_window: 10m`
liz: also recommend a new dashboard row: `Alerts by grouping_key` and a throttling widget for PD traffic
incident-bot: RESOLVE: ORIGIN:host-12 - error-rate normalized after reroute and runtime patch - alert volume reduced below threshold
sara (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. leaving a 1-hour watch window. oncall-next take over final verification
oncall-next: taking over. will keep an eye until +1h
michael: for post-incident, we should run a short eval to verify quality didn't regress from reroutes/host drains
sara (oncall): agreed. capture evals and schedule a brief sync tomorrow with eng-runtime and srep
liz: adding notes to postmortem template. will include timeline and the temporary alert config diffs
sara (oncall): final note: PD noise reduced immediately after squelch; main action item is durable grouping + dedupe in config + dashboard to spot noisy hosts faster. closing thread but keep follow-ups in #incidents
